items.title: Cave Diver
items.html:
Cave Diver

Ranger subclass

Level 3: Subterranean Adept

From your experiences in caves you gain the following features:
Rock climber. You gain a 40ft climbing speed.
Spelunker. You can fit in a space the size of a creature one size smaller without squeezing, and a creature two sizes smaller (but not tiny) while squeezing.
Mineral knowledge. When you make a check to determine the value of an unworked mineral, gem, or rock, you have advantage on the check.

Level 3: Cave Diver Spells

Your connection to the underground has granted the following spells.

Ranger Level Spell
3rd Disguise self
5th Darkvision
9th Meld into stone
13th Stoneskin
17th Wall of stone

You always have these spells prepared.

Level 7: Cave's Stride

You have learned how to move in caves expertly and can move through caves really fast. You gain the following benefits:
Space is unnecessary. Your speed isn't halved when squeezing to fit in a space.
Stone pusher. You have advantage on any check to move a rock, short of an attack roll.
Stone's Speed. Your movement speed increases by 5ft.

Level 11: Cave Disaster Master

You have gained skills to avoid disasters while cave diving; you gain the following benefits:
Fall catch. When you're falling, you can use a reaction to halve the fall damage.
See it first. You gain darkvision out to 120ft and blindsight out to 10ft. If you already have darkvision, its radius increases by 120ft.
Weakness finder. You have advantage on any check to find cracks or weak spots in caves and stone structures.

Level 15: Ultimate Cave Diver

You have spent so much time in the caves you are a master at spelunking. You gain the following benefits:
Expert climber. Your climbing speed increases to 50ft.
Rock solid. You gain resistance to non-magical bludgeoning damage.
Spelunking master. You and your party (if you lead) can no longer get lost in a cave; additionally, you can sustain yourself with enough food and water to survive 7 days in a cave.

items.title: Charming Domain
items.html:
Charming Domain

Cleric subclass

Clerics that are a part of the charming domain have high charisma and generally follow the deities Aphrodite, Apollo, Loki, etc. They are very good at charming others and good at resisting it themselves. They also generally have chaotic alignments.

Charming domain spells

Cleric level       spells
1st       Charm person, Command
3rd       Crown of madness, Suggestion
5th       Enemies abound, Hypnotic Pattern
7th       Compulsion, Dominate Monster
9th       Dominate person, Geas

Bonus Cantrip

At 1st level you always know the Friends cantrip and it doesn't count against your known cantrips.

Ability Score Improvement

Also at 1st level your charisma score increases by one.

Channel Divinity: Charming Aura

Starting at 2nd level you can use your channel divinity to make you and your party look better.
As an action, you can present your holy symbol and gain a 10 ft. aura around you for 5 minutes that gives you and anyone of your choice in range +2 to charisma and when they force a creature to make a saving throw to not be charmed a -2 to the roll.

Crazy Charmer

Starting at 6th level any and all saving throws a creature makes to not be charmed by you always has -4 to the roll.

Absurd Charming

At 8th level, your charming becomes even more irresistible, whenever you force a creature to make a saving throw to not be charmed, you can force them to instead of making a wisdom saving throw to make a saving throw of any other mental stat.
You can use this ability 3 times per long rest.
You also gain immunity to being charmed.

Master Charmer

Starting at 17th level, all saving throws to not be charmed by you always have disadvantage.
Your aura also gives immunity to being charmed.

items.title: Circle of the Sky
items.html:
Circle of the Sky

Druid subclass

Level 3: Circle of the Sky Spells

Druid Level Prepared Spells
3rd Feather fall, fog cloud, gust, thunderwave, warding wind
5th Sleet storm, wind wall
7th Ice storm, call lightning
9th Cloudkill, control winds
17th Storm of vengeance

You always have these spells prepared.

Level 3: Lift to the Sky

As a bonus action, you can expend a use of your wild shape to call the winds and gain the following benefits for 10 minutes or until you choose to end it (no action required).
Windswept. Both your movement speed and your jump height increase by 10ft.
Wind control. You can cast gust or fog cloud as a bonus action.
Unmoving. When you are moved against your will (such as shoving) you can use a reaction to not be moved.

Level 6: Avatar of the Sky

While your lift to the sky feature is active you also gain the following benefits.
Touch the sky. You gain a flying speed equal to your speed.
Gaseous. You gain resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

Level 10: Sky's Mastery

Mastery from the sky gains you mastery in some elements. Choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, lightning, or thunder
You have resistance to it, and whenever you deal damage of that type, treat a 1 on a damage die as a 2.
Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change your choice.

Level 14: From the Sky

You now gain a free use of your lift to the sky feature, which you regain when you finish a long rest, and while it's active you gain the following benefits:
Wind quick. Your fly speed increases to 50ft.
Sky's affinity. You have immunity to the damage type you chose for your Sky's Mastery feature.
Sky's fortitude. Whenever you cast a circle of the sky spell, you or an ally within 30 ft of you gains a number of temporary hit points equal to your level + your wisdom modifier.

items.title: College of Glass Breakers
items.html:
College of Glass Breakers

Bard subclass

Some Bards who join the college of glass breakers think they are good at singing but are really bad. Others know they sing terribly, and embrace it. Bards in the college of glass breakers are much better at dancing and playing music than singing. At high levels, even doing simple tasks involving a little singing, can cause nearby creatures to take psychic damage.

Level 3: Psychic Mastery

Whenever you deal psychic damage, you can add your charisma modifier. Additionally, you can also expend a use of your bardic inspiration, to roll the die and add it to the damage.

Level 3: Destructive

You have gotten good at breaking things; whenever you roll any kind of damage against an object or construct, treat a 1 as a 2.

Level 6: Have Heard Worse

From hearing yourself sing, you are affected less by mind hurting sounds. You gain resistance to psychic damage.

Level 14: Glass Breaking Song

Whenever you cast a spell that has a verbal component, or as a bonus action on your turn, you can force all creatures within 30 ft of you to succeed an intelligence saving throw, or take 4d8 psychic damage.
Any glass object within range has a 50 percent chance of shattering. Any creature who cannot hear you automatically succeeds the saving throw. You can use this feature twice per long rest, unless you expend a use of your bardic inspiration to restore one use (no action required).

items.title: Gadgeteer
items.html:
Gadgeteer

Artificer subclass

Level 3

Tool Proficiency. Gain proficiency in tinkers tools. If you already proficiency in tinker's tools gain proficiency in an artisan tool set of your choice.
Extended Spell List.

Artificer Level Spells
3rd Mage Armor, Tenser's Floating Disk
5th Cloud of Daggers, Knock
9th Phantom Steed, Sending
13th Evard's Black Tentacles, Wall of Fire
17th Hold Monster, Wall of Force

Gadget Smith.
Choose 3 of the listed gadgets to learn how to make.
You can activate a gadget as an action or bonus action if it is within 30 ft of you and can deactivate it as an action if it is within your reach. Gadgets also break down after 1 min of use. Gadget effects only take place while the gadget is activated.
During a long rest, if you have tinkers tools you may make 1 gadget or repair 2. You may only have a number of working gadgets equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).
Each time you level up choose 1 gadget to learn or level up.

  • Regenerator: Each creature within 5 ft of the regenerator heals 1d4 HP at the start of their turn. +1d4 per gadget level.
  • Force Dome: a 5 ft radius see through dome surrounds the gadget. When you activate this gadget you may form an opening in the dome. If the dome is reduced to 0 HP the gadget is deactivated and destroyed. The dome is immune to all non magical damage, resistant to all damage, and has HP equal to 5x your INT (minimum 1). +5x your INT (minimum 1) HP.
  • Instant Wall: a 5 ft wide, 30 ft long, and 20 ft tall wall appears from the gadget. If a creature is occupying a space that the wall takes up, the creature takes 3d10 force damage and moves to the nearest unoccupied space. If the wall is reduced to 0 HP the gadget is deactivated and destroyed. The wall is immune to all non magical damage, resistant to all damage, and has HP equal to 5x your INT (minimum 1). +5x your INT (minimum 1) HP.
  • Auto-Turret: When you activate this gadget you may designate creatures for the turret to not target. The turret takes its turn after yours. The turret will attack the nearest creature within range on its turn. Gun: INT+PB to hit, (60/120), (1d6+INT) piercing damage. +1d6 piercing damage per level.
  • Manual Turret: When you activate this gadget you or any creature you designate may make attacks with it. Attack rolls made with this use DEX and gain a bonus equal to your INT. Gun: DEX(user's)+INT(yours)+PB(yours) to hit, (60/120), (1d6+DEX(user's)+INT(yours)).
  • Damage Emitter: Each creature within 10 ft of the gadget takes 2d6 of a damage type you choose when you activate it. +1d6 damage per level.
  • Temporal Decelerator: Each creature within up to 5 ft (you choose the radius when you activate the gadget) of the gadget is slowed granting them disadvantage on dexterity saving throws originating from outside the radius, disadvantage on attack rolls targeting creatures outside the radius, creatures outside the radius have advantage on attack rolls targeting creatures inside the radius, and each creature inside the aura has its speed halved. +5 ft max radius per level.
  • Temporal Accelerator: Each creature within up to 5 ft (you choose the radius when you activate the gadget) of the gadget is sped up granting them advantage on dexterity saving throws originating from outside the radius, advantage on attack rolls targeting creatures outside the radius, creatures outside the radius have disadvantage on attack rolls targeting creatures inside the radius, and each creature inside the aura has its speed doubled. +5 ft max radius per level.
  • Earthquaker: The ground in a 10 ft radius around this gadget becomes difficult terrain and each creature in the difficult terrain caused by this gadget must make a DEX ST at the start of its turn against your spell save DC. On a fail the creature is knocked prone.
  • Teleporter: As a bonus action you may teleport to the location of the teleporter if you are within 30 ft of the teleporter. +30 ft range per level.

Level 5

Quick Fix. Once per day you may repair a gadget you are holding as an action.
Infused Gadget. You may use one of your infusions to make a gadget. Gadgets made this way do not break down.

Level 9

More Gadgets. You may now have an additional number of gadgets made equal to your PB.

Level 15

Empowering Gadgets. Gain a bonus to your movement speed equal to twice the number of gadgets you have activated.

items.title: Oath of Drug Dealing
items.html:
Oath of Drug Dealing

Paladin Subclass

Oath of Drug Dealing Spells

Paladin Level Spells
3rd Dissonant Whispers, Hideous Laughter
5th Darkness(Smoke Grenade), Blindness/Deafness
9th Stinking Cloud, Haste
13th Confusion, Phantasmal Killer
17th Cloudkill, Contagion

You always have these spells prepared.

Channel Divinity: Brewing Drugs

At the end of a long rest, you brew some drugs. As a Bonus action, you may expend a use of Channel divinity to administer the drugs to a creature you can touch, granting the creature one of the effects of your choice from the list below.

  • Heal a number of d4s equal to your paladin level
  • The creature gains an additional bonus action on each of its turns for 1 minute
  • The creature takes a number of d4s of Psychic or Poison damage (your choice) on a failed CON saving throw against your spell save DC or half as much on a success.
  • The creature gains advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened for 1 hour
  • The creature gains the paralyzed condition for 1 minute
  • The creature's speed increases or decreases (your choice) by 5 times your CHA modifier for 1 minute

Aura of Drug Tolerance

Starting at 7th level, you constantly emanate drugs from your person, giving those around you drug tolerance while you're not incapacitated. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. Creatures of your choice within your aura gain resistance to Acid, Poison, or Psychic damage. You may change the damage type on a short or long rest.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30ft.

Skilled Brewer

Starting at 15th level, crafting consumable items costs half as many resources and requires half as much time for you.

Drug Master

As a Bonus Action, you gain the benefits below for 1 minute or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a 5th level spell slot (no action required).

  • Intolerance Aura. When an enemy ends its turn in your aura, it must make a CON Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the creature gains vulnerability to poison or psychic damage and loses resistance to that damage type if it has resistance to that damage type until the end of its next turn. However, if it has immunity to the damage type, it remains unaffected.
  • Instant Brew. As a Bonus Action on your turn, you may craft a consumable item that you have the resources to craft.
  • Panacea. When you heal a creature, you may choose to double the amount of HP that is regained by the creature.

items.title: Path Of The BIG Monke
items.html:
Path Of The BIG Monke

Barbarian Subclass

3rd Level: Resourceful

Your time spent in the wilderness has made you very resourceful, you gain proficiency in improvised weapons. Your unarmed strikes gain a d6 damage die. Your unarmed strike damage die increases to a d8 at 6th level, a d10 at 10th level and a d12 at 14th level.

3rd Level: Monkey Mad

You can go into a monkey rage when you rage, doing so causes your body to transform into that of a large monkey. For the duration of your rage, you gain the following benefits;

  • Your size increases to Large
  • You can make an unarmed strike as a bonus action.
  • You can move a creature you are grappling at full speed if it is at least one size smaller than you.
  • You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, if you already have a climbing speed, cry about it.
  • The reach of your melee attacks increases by 5 feet.

However the transformation makes it hard for your monkey brain to understand how to use modern weapons. While you are raging, you do not add your proficiency bonus to attack rolls made with martial weapons.

6th Level: Monkey Fists

Monkey Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Constitution Modifier
Once per turn When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon you can force them to make a constitution saving throw against your monkey save DC. On a failed save, the target is stunned until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses after a short or long rest.
While you are raging, you now deal double damage to objects and structures. Your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity.

10th Level: Monkey Make a Noise

When you enter a Monkey Rage, you can let out a loud and intimidating Monkey noise. Every hostile creature within 30 ft of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Monkey save DC. Creatures that succeed their save suffer no effects. Creatures that fail their save become frightened for 1-minute. Frightened creatures can repeat the saving throw at the end of their turn. This feature can be used once per short or long rest.

items.title: Path of the Otherworldly Warrior
items.html:
Path of the Otherworldly Warrior

Barbarian Subclass

Rage with the power of another plane of existence.
Barbarians that take the Path of the Otherworldly Warrior are imbued with power of the elements or power from outer planes. They generally share at least a similar alignment with the plane. High level barbarians take on aspects of the plane and unleash the wrath of these planes.

Level 3: Aspect of the Planes

At 3rd level you channel your rage from another plane which affects other features. Choose a plane from the plane table to determine these effects.

Planes of existence

Plane Damage Type Language
Abyss Acid Abyssal
Carceri Cold Void Speech
Limbo Force Deep Speech
Mechanus Force Thri-kreen
Mount Celestia Radiant Celestial
Nine Hells Fire Infernal
Pandemonium Thunder Deep Speech
Feywild Psychic Sylvan
Shadowfell Necrotic Undercommon
Elemental plane of fire Fire Ignan
Elemental plane of earth Force Terran
Elemental plane of water Cold Aquan
Elemental plane of air Thunder Auran

You know the language associated with that plane, and while you're raging, you have resistance to and your rage damage bonus is that damage type.

Level 3: Planar Spells

You learn a spell based on the plane you chose:
Abyss, Carceri, Limbo, Mechanus, Mount Celestia, Nine Hells, Pandemonium, Feywild, or Shadowfell:
You know the find familiar spell and can cast it only as a ritual. Rather than the normal options, your familiar is determined by the plane you chose and is an imp (Nine Hells), homunculus (Mecanus), quasit (Abyss), Dretch (Carceri), skeleton (Shadowfell), slaad tadpole (Limbo or Pandemonium), sphinx of wonder (Mount Celestia), or sprite (Feywild). But unlike normal, your familiar can attack.
An Elemental Plane:
You always have the Armor of Agathy's spell prepared and instead of its normal damage type, it deals the type of damage associated with the plane you chose. You can cast it even when raging. You can cast it a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Level 6: Rage of the Planes

At 6th level, whenever you rage you can choose and gain one of the following options:
Attacks of the Planes:
The first time on each of your turns you hit a creature with an attack, the attack does the damage type associated with the plane you chose instead of its normal damage type.
Movement of the Planes:
Difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement. Additionally, you can spend half your movement speed to exit any non-magical restraints.
Mastery of the Planes:
Whenever you hit an attack with a weapon you have mastery with, you can use any other mastery property instead.

Level 10: Otherworldly Attacking

At 10th level, while you are raging you are a weapon master; all weapon attacks you make use a die size up (d6 to d8 and d8 to d10 and so forth), if it is a d12 use 2d6 instead of a d20. For a weapon that already uses more than one die, increase just one. Your unarmed strikes now do a d4. Additionally, you can now wield two handed weapons in just one hand.

Level 14: Planar Presence

At 14th level, when you rage (lasting for the duration of the rage), you can gain one of the following effects:
Planar Immunity:
You take on a form as an aspect of the plane. You have immunity to the damage type associated with the plane you chose.
Planar Doom:
Every creature of your choice within 30 ft of you must succeed a dex saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and your proficiency bonus) or take a number of d4s of the damage associated with the plane you chose equal to your rage bonus. You can use a bonus action on your turn to cause this again.
Pain of the Plane:
Any damage you do of the type associated with the plan you chose is doubled.

You can use this feature one time per long rest unless you expend a use of your rage to restore it (no action required).

items.title: Warrior of the Wild
items.html:
Warrior of the Wild

Monk Subclass

Warriors of the Wild have embraced nature and harness it to cast spells, protect people, and even unleash its wrath on people. It is a unique subclass that is a ⅓ caster not using the wizard spell list.

Level 3: Spellcasting

You have learned to cast spells from embracing nature.
Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. Thunderclap and Thorn Whip are recommended.
When you reach Monk level 10, you learn another cantrip from the Druid spell list.
Spell Slots. The Warrior of the Wild Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a long rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the Druid spell list. Thunderwave, Entangle, and Faerie Fire are recommended.
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warrior of the Wild Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Druid spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Monk, your list of prepared spells can include five Druid spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Druid spell for which you have spell slots.
Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.
Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Druid spells.

Level 3: Spell Slot Regeneration

You have learned how to turn your focus into spell slots. On your turn (no action required) you can convert Ki / Focus Points into spell slots; expending the required amount of points into a slot of that level. You cannot have more spell slots than your maximum of that level.
You can also expend a spell slot of that level to gain points equal to the cost. You still cannot have more than your maximum. You cannot create a slot you don't have already (e.g. you cannot make 4th Level slots until you are 19 level).

Creating Spell Slots

Level 6: Wild Attacks

Whenever you take the attack action or use your Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Druid cantrips that has a casting time of an action. You can do this once per turn.

Level 11: Nature's Shield

When you or an ally within 30 ft of you is hit with an attack, you can use a reaction and expend 4 Ki / Focus Points to make a plant shield appear in front of that creature. The plant shield grants +5 to AC until the start of your next turn, potentially turning a hit into a miss. If any creature hits the target while they have the shield with an attack, the attacker takes 2d10 piercing damage.

Level 17: Wrath of Nature

Whenever you hit a melee attack with a Monk weapon or an unarmed strike, you can invoke nature's wrath. You expend 7 Ki / Focus Points and the target of the attack takes an additional 4d10 piercing damage, as vines whip them. If the target is large or smaller, the target then has to make a strength saving throw (DC equals your spell DC). If the target fails, the target is then restrained. If the target succeeds, is huge or is gargantuan, it takes an additional 2d10 piercing damage. A restrained creature takes 1d10 piercing damage at the start of each of their turns, and can make a strength (athletics) check against your spell DC, freeing itself on a success.


Variant Warrior of the Wild

A different way to deal with spells as a monk.

Level 3: Spellcasting

You have embraced nature's power and have gained access to spells regarding it. You know 2 druid cantrips, and learn another at monk level 10.
You also know some level 1+ spells from the druid spell list. The number of spells and the max level is determined by your level.

Level 3: Nature's Points

You gain an additional amount of Ki/Focus points equal to your wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

Level 6: Nature's Obscuration

Whenever you hit a melee attack with a Monk weapon or an unarmed strike, you can expend 2 Ki/Focus points to cause the target to make a dexterity saving throw (DC equals your spell DC) or have the blinded condition. Additionally, you gain +2 AC against that creature until the start of your next turn.

Level 11: Nature's Shield

When you or an ally within 30 ft of you is hit with an attack, you can use a reaction and expend 4 Ki / Focus Points to make a plant shield appear in front of that creature. The plant shield grants +5 to AC until the start of your next turn, potentially turning a hit into a miss. items.title: Jack of All Trades
items.html:
Jack of All Trades

Master of none

A homebrew 2024 class

Characters who are a Jack of all trades have a little skill in everything. They're heavy skill monkeys and have lots of variety in features and techniques for battle. Jack of All Trades comes with a lot of choices, so indecisive people could take forever to make a character with this class. Example builds can be found here.

Note: if any feature you gain from another place (class or subclass) mentions your level in that class but you gained the feature in this class, use this class’ level instead.

Core Jack of All Trades Features

Primary ability Any
Hit point die D8 per level
Saving throw proficiencies Choose 1 of dexterity, wisdom, or constitution; and 1 of strength, intelligence, or charisma.
Skill proficiencies Choose any 4
Weapon proficiencies Simple and martial weapons
Tool proficiencies Choose 3 tools (including instruments individually)
Armor training Light and medium armor, shields
Starting equipment Choose A, B, C, or D: (A) Leather Armor, arcane/ druidic focus (quarterstaff) or a holy symbol (amulet), shortsword, 2 daggers, book (a trade skill), dungeoneer's pack, tool of your choice (one of which you're proficient), and 20 gp; (B) hide armor, shield, longsword, shortbow, 20 arrows, quiver, explorer's pack, 2 handaxes, tool of your choice (one of which you're proficient), and 4 gp; (C) quarterstaff, 2 daggers, scimitar, 10 darts, burglar's pack, tool of your choice (one of which you're proficient), and 15gp; or (D) 116 gp;

Multiclassing in Jack of All Trades:

Gain the following features from the table: Hit point die, proficiency in 2 skills and tools (total), and training with light and medium armor.

For features like Dabbling in all Classes, you cannot pick features you already have, even if it's from a different class; except for the spell casting feature: treat it as if this class was the class giving the spellcasting feature and use the spellcasting multiclass rules.

Multiclassing out of Jack of All Trades:

You cannot multiclass into a class that you took its version of the spellcasting or weapon mastery feature. If you have any feature given by only one class at level 10 or lower, you cannot take the class that gives that feature.

Class Features:

Level 1: Dabbling in All Classes

Choose 2 different features from other classes granted at 1st level from the list below. You gain that feature. If multiple classes are listed for it, choose which class’s version to use. You still can only pick it once. (For the purpose of Jack of All Trades rules affecting spellcasting, consider pact magic a spellcasting feature).

  • Rage
  • Unarmored defense (barbarian or monk)
  • Spellcasting (artificer, ranger, or paladin) / pact magic
  • Second wind
  • Martial Arts
  • Weapon mastery (paladin, ranger, or rogue)
  • Lay on hands
  • Favored enemy
  • Expertise
  • Tinker’s magic
  • Bardic inspiration
  • Psionic Power (UA Psion)
  • Subtle Telekinesis (UA Psion)
  • Divine order
  • Primal order

Level 2: Expertise

You gain expertise in 2 skills or tools you already have proficiency in. You gain this feature again at levels 7 and 15.

Level 3: Jack of All Trades Subclass

You gain a subclass, which are listed below. Your options are: Sentinel, Sage, Competition Meister, Performer, and The Jack of All Jacks.

Some have prerequisites, which require you to have picked a version of said feature for Dabbling in All Classes.

Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the ability score improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Jack of All Trades levels 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16.

Level 5: More Dabbling in All Classes

Choose 2 more features from the Dabbling in All Classes feature; with the list below included. You gain that feature.

  • Extra attack (barbarian, fighter, monk, paladin, or ranger)
  • Fast movement
  • Faithful steed
  • Uncanny dodge
  • Wild companion
  • Deflect attacks
  • Fighting style (fighter, paladin, or ranger)
  • Jack of All Trades
  • Danger sense
  • Reckless Attack
  • Deft Explorer
  • Font of Magic (prerequisite: Spellcasting/Pact Magic)
  • Metamagic (prerequisite: Font of Magic)
  • Psionic Restoration (UA Psion, prerequisite: Psionic Power)
  • Scholar

Level 11: Even More Dabbling in All Classes

Choose 2 more features from the More Dabbling in All Classes feature; with the list below included. You gain that feature.

  • Reliable talent
  • Evasion (monk or rogue)
  • Tactical Master
  • Acrobatic movement
  • Radiant strikes
  • Two extra attacks (prerequisite: extra attack feature)
  • Flash of genius
  • Feral Instinct
  • Magic item Adept
  • Self-restoration

Level 17: Master Artisan

You are a master of the trades and gain proficiency in all tools.

In addition, you gain expertise in 2 tools.

Level 18: Dabbled in All

Choose 1 feature from the Even More Dabbling in All Classes feature; with the list below included. You gain that feature.

  • Indomitable Might
  • Feral Senses
  • Elusive
  • Studied attacks
  • Magic item Master
  • Nature's Veil
  • Slippery Mind

Level 19: Epic Boon

You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Boon of Skill is recommended.

items.title: Oath of the Protector
items.html:
Oath of the Protector

Paladin subclass

Level 3: Uncanny Protection

When a creature within 30 feet of you gets hit with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to expend a use of your Channel Divinity to give that creature +5 to AC, potentially turning the hit into a miss.

Level 3: Oath of the Protector Spells

Your oath grants you the following spells.

Paladin Level Spells
3rd Shield of Faith, Protection from Evil and Good
5th Aid, Protection from Poison
9th Protection from Energy, Beacon of Hope
13th Death Ward, Stoneskin
17th Antilife Shell, Dispel Evil and Good

You always have these spells prepared.

Level 7: Aura of Increased Protection

Your Aura of Protection now grants a +2 bonus to AC.
Additionally, when you or a creature within your aura gets hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses after a short or long rest.

Level 15: Abjuration Specialist

Whenever you cast a spell from the Abjuration school of magic, it doesn't require concentration and instead lasts for its full duration.
Additionally, you can prepare one extra Abjuration spell from any spell list without it counting against your total number of spells prepared.

Level 20: Protector of All

As a bonus action, you can empower yourself with protective power for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:
Masterful Defense. When you or a creature within your aura is hit with a melee attack, the creature hit can use its reaction to reduce the damage by one damage die (for example, reducing 2d6+3 to 1d6+3), ignoring static bonuses.
Shared Defense. As a bonus action on consecutive turns, you can give yourself a penalty to AC (minimum 1) to grant a creature within your Aura of Protection a bonus to AC equal to the penalty plus half your Charisma modifier (minimum +3).
Saving Throw Proficiencies. Each creature of your choice within your aura gains proficiency in one saving throw of its choice, losing that proficiency when it leaves your aura or when this effect ends.

You can use this feature once per long rest unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to restore its use (no action required).

items.title: Tactician
items.html:
Tactician

Wizard subclass

Level 3: Intelligently Mobile

You have learned how to use your surroundings to do athletic things efficiently. Whenever you make an athletics, acrobatics, or stealth check, you gain a bonus equal to your Intelligence modifier.

Additionally your walking speed increases by 5ft.

Level 3: Levin Sword

You gain a cool electric sword, called a Levin sword. The Levin sword counts as a longsword, but does an extra 1d6 lightning damage. Only you can use it, and you always have proficiency with it.

The Levin sword becomes more powerful at certain levels, with the lightning damage increasing to 1d12 at 7th level, 3d6 at 13, and 3d8 at 18.

If you lose your Levin sword, you can complete a 10 minute ritual to gain a new one.

Level 6: Spell Tomes

You gain the ability to make special tomes for casting spells. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can create a number of tomes equal to half your proficiency bonus (round down). You can choose a spell in your spellbook from one of the schools of magic listed below to put in the tome. On your turn, holding one of these tomes you may cast that spell without expending a spell slot. The max spell level is 3rd and increases at certain levels: 9 (4th), 13 (5th), 16 (6th), 20 (7th). The total of all the spell’s levels cannot be greater than your proficiency bonus plus your Intelligence modifier.

After a spell has been cast from a tome or you finish another long rest, the tome crumbles to dust.

The schools you can choose are: evocation, transmutation, or necromancy.

Level 10: Master of All Tactics

You have become a master of tactics and battle maneuvers. Your walking speed increases by another 5ft, and whenever you make an athletics, acrobatics, or stealth check, you gain a bonus equal to double your Intelligence modifier.

Additionally, whenever you move or make a melee attack roll within 5ft of an ally, they can use a reaction to move up to half their walking speed. This movement ignores opportunity attacks.

Level 14: Knight's Service

Once per day, as an action, you can call a knight to your service. They appear at an unoccupied spot within 10ft of you. They use the knight stat block except for it lacks the heavy crossbow action and drops no gear. They exist until you take a long rest or you or they die. They are an ally to you, and they take their turn right after yours.

Additionally, on your turn, if you take the ready action, are within 10ft of your knight and on the knight's next turn lands at least one attack, you can do a chain attack. The triggering attack only does 5 damage.

The chain attack includes the knight doing a number of attacks equal to 1 + half your Intelligence modifier (minimum 2, maximum 4) and you doing a number of spell attacks equal to half your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1, maximum 3). None of the attacks include any bonuses and your spell attacks do one of the following damage types: fire, lightning, slashing or necrotic.

Finally, if at least half (round up) of the total amount of attacks hit, you can do a killing blow. The target makes a CON saving throw (DC equals your spell DC), instantly killing the target (if they end with less than 50 hp), or knocking them unconscious on a fail.

The chain attack kills the knight when it finishes.

items.title: War Sorcery
items.html:
War Sorcery

Dominate and power over others in battle

Sorcerer subclass

Whether you were blessed by a war god, inherited it from a powerful creature, or was exposed to a magically scarred battlefield, you gained powerful war magic. It gives you power to dominate and alter a battlefield.

Level 3: Battlefield Warping

You gain the ability to warp a battlefield to turn the tides in your favor. On your turn, as a bonus action, you can choose two creatures that are within 60ft of you. An unwilling creature makes a CON saving throw (DC equals your spell DC). If all unwilling creatures fail or both are willing, the two creatures then switch places.

You can use this feature a number of times per long rest equal to your charisma modifier.

Level 3: War Sorcery Spells

You always have the following spells prepared.

Sorcerer level Spells
3 Spellfire Flare, Chromatic Orb, Flame Blade, Mind Spike
5 Conjure Barrage, Erupting Earth
7 Doomtide, Ice Storm
9 Destructive Wave, Flame Strike

Level 6: Beat Down Metamagic

Having improved shaping your magic for war, you gain the following metamagic option and it doesn’t count towards the amount you know.

Beat Down Spell

Cost: 3 sorcery points

When you cast a spell that does damage to a creature, you can expend 3 sorcery points to increase the spell's damage. The spell increases in damage by the spell's level +1 and another roll of its highest damage die (7 for a set amount/no dice to roll).

You can use Beat Down Spell even if you've already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

Level 14: Spell Explosions

Your spells have become particularly destructive and great for battle. Whenever you cast a sorcerer spell that does damage with a spell slot, you can choose one of the following modifications to apply.

Damage explosion. You can use Beat Down Metamagic without expending sorcery points.

**Area explosion **(only with an AOE spell). The AOE increases in an additional 10ft sphere, somewhere touching the original AOE.

**Accurate explosion. **If it has a saving throw, all creatures have disadvantage on one.

**Unavoidable explosion. **Any creature targeted by the spell gains no bonus from half or three quarters cover.

You can use this feature 3 times per long rest, unless you expend 3 sorcery points to restore a use of it.

Level 18: War Magic Mastery

You have mastered you war magic and gain the following features:

**Improved Battlefield Warping. **When you use your battlefield warping feature, you can now choose to also deal 1d6 force damage to either or both of the target creatures.

**Improved Beat Down Spell. **The first time per long rest you use Beat Down Spell, it only costs 1 sorcery point.

**Improved Spell Explosions. **The first time per long rest you use your Spell Explosions feature, you can choose 2 options instead of 1.

**Earth Destruction. **You always have the earthquake spell prepared.

items.title: Life Leech
items.html:
Life Leech

Rogue Subclass

Life Leeches specialize in stealing life essence rather than material goods. At higher levels, they can even bolster themselves and their allies with this new-stolen life force.

Level 3: Life Leeching Sneak Attack

Whenever you roll damage for an attack that adds your sneak attack damage, add an additional 1d6 necrotic damage, as you now channel negative energy through your attacks.

Level 3: Pool of Negative Energy

You now channel negative energy that is stored in negative energy points. Your max number of points is your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus + your rogue level. You regain all points at the end of a long rest. You can use the points in the following ways:

Negative Fortitude: As a bonus action, you expend any number of points (minimum of 1, maximum of your rogue level), to gain that many temp HP.

**Life Leech Strike: **As an action, if you have a free hand, you may expend 2 points to strike at an enemy within 30ft of you. The strike counts as a ranged weapon (you are proficient), dealing 1d6 slashing damage on a hit. The strike qualifies for Sneak Attack as long as you meet the other requirements. The strike doesn't give off your location if you are hidden.

**Negative Energy Spells: **You can spend a number of points equal to the number associated with the spell to cast one of the following spells. You must be at a minimum rogue level listed to choose a spell.

Your spellcasting ability for your rogue spells is intelligence.

Spell Point Cost Minimum Rogue Level
Chill Touch 2 3
Toll the Dead 2 3
Arms of Hadar 4 7
Wrathful Smite 6 7
Wither and Bloom 6 13
Hunger of Hadar 10 19

Level 9: Life Leech Empowerment

Your life leeching has improved and now empowers you. Whenever you deal the extra damage with Life Leeching Sneak Attack, you regain a number of negative energy points equal to the amount of necrotic damage dealt.

Level 13: Shared Life Leech Empowerment

Immediately after you gain negative energy points from your Life Leech Empowerment (still using a bonus action) you may use your Negative Fortitude, except a willing creature within 30ft gains the temp HP instead.

Level 17: Master of Life Leeching

Your abilities are honed on stealing life force, increasing your Life Leeching Sneak Attack and your Life Leech Strike damage to 1d10.

Additionally, casting the spells chill touch and toll the dead with the Negative Energy Spells feature now don't cost any points.

Finally, Life Leech Empowerment always gives a minimum of 4 points.

items.title: Sentinel
items.html:
Sentinel

Protect in anyway necessary

Level 3: Steel Defense

When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can grant yourself a bonus to your AC up to +5 until the start of your next turn. Until the end of your next turn, any attack you make has a penalty to the attack roll equal to the bonus to your AC.

You can use this feature once per round.

Level 3: Strike Back

When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use a reaction to make a melee attack against that creature, ignoring any bonus to the attack and damage. Advantage doesn't count as a bonus.

Level 9: Magical Defenses

You learn the shield spell. You can cast it a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Level 13: Shared Defense

When a creature within 30 ft of you is targeted by an attack roll, you can use a reaction to use your Steel Defense feature. The creature attacked gains the bonus, but you keep the penalty.

Level 20: Guardian

When you use your Shared Defense or Steel Defense feature, you can remove the penalty. You can also either gain an additional 1d6 bonus, or make it not require a reaction. You still can only do it once per round.

You can use this feature 3 times per long rest.

items.title: Sage
items.html:
Sage

Delve in all kinds of magic secrets

Prerequisite: spellcasting/pact magic

Level 3: Spell Knowledge

Choose 2 spells of a level you can cast from any spell list. You always have those prepared and they don't count towards your prepared spells.

Whenever you gain a level you can change one of these spells.

Level 3: Magically Observant

You gain proficiency in Arcana and Perception, and expertise in one of the two.

Additionally, you gain advantage on any other kind of check to observe something magical.

Level 9: Master of a School

Choose a school of magic, any spell you cast from that school, gains a bonus to its attack rolls and saving throws equal to half your spellcasting modifier. If the spell doesn't have either, its damage increases by that amount. Otherwise, nothing changes.

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change your option.

Level 13: Speed Caster

On your turn, you may change a spell's casting time to a bonus action if its normal casting time is an action.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting modifier per long rest.

Level 20: Master Mage

On your turn you may cast another leveled-spell if one of the spells casting time is a bonus action or you use your Speed Caster feature.

You can use this feature twice per long rest and regain one use after a short rest. You can expend a 5th level spell slot to restore a use (no action required).

Variant Sage (Dark Sage)

All features are the same except Spell Knowledge and Magically Observant; replace them with the following features.

Level 3: Shadowy Magic

Gain 2 eldritch invocations, as described in the warlock feature.

Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one invocation with another which you qualify.

Level 3: Siphon Life

Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature with a spell you regain 1d10 hit points and gain 1d6 temporary hit points.

items.title: Competition Meister
items.html:
Competition Meister

Be a master in any kind of sport, physical or otherwise

Prerequisite: 1 of the following: unarmored defense, second wind, weapon mastery, or magical tinkering

Level 3: Natural

Being a natural in athletics and any competition, you gain proficiency in 2 of the following skills: athletics, acrobatics, deception, or performance. You also gain proficiency in 2 gaming sets.

Level 3: Sport Weapon Bonus

You are amazing at using weapons used in sports, such as a javelin. When throwing or using any of the weapons listed below, you can add +1 to attack rolls and its range increases by 10ft if it is thrown or a ranged weapon (both short and long). If the weapon must be used in a specific way it is listed in parentheses.

The weapons are: handaxe (thrown), javelin (thrown), dart, shortbow, lance (mounted only), blowgun, longbow, rapier, light hammer, pistol, musket, heavy crossbow, light crossbow.

Level 9: Strategist

Having strategized and thought 10 steps ahead, you become more aware of surrounding danger. You gain advantage on dexterity saving throws that you can see the origin as long as you're not incapacitated.

You also gain proficiency in investigation and intelligence saving throws.

Level 13: Comeback for Everything

Learning how to deal with anything an opponent may throw at you, you gain the following features.

Stay back. When a creature moves within your reach of an unarmed strike, you can use a reaction to make an unarmed strike as long as you pick the shove option, and push them 5ft.

Block. When a creature hits you with an attack, you can use a reaction to add +2 to your AC until the start of your next turn; provided you're holding something.

Interrupt. Whenever a creature within 5ft of you takes the ready action, you can use a reaction to cause them to make an intelligence saving throw (DC equals 8 + your dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus), losing the readied action on a fail.

Mental shield. Whenever you are subjected to an effect that forces you to make a charisma, intelligence, or wisdom saving throw, you can use a reaction to grant yourself advantage on the roll.

Level 20: Winner of All

You have competed in all kinds of competitions, gaining you proficiency in any check to compete in any kind of game or sport.

You gain resistance in 2 damage types other than bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing.

Additionally, you have become hardier and your hit point maximum increases by 20.

items.title: Performer
items.html:
Performer

Be a master of the stage and a sight to behold

Level 3: Performance Dice

You gain special dice in a pool called performance dice. These dice are used for this feature and other features, you gain more and they increase in size at certain levels as shown in the table below.

You regain one die after a short rest and regain all dice when you finish a long rest.

Jack of All Trades Level Number of performance dice Die size
3 4 D6
5 6 D8
9 8 D8
11 8 D10
13 10 D10
17 12 D12

You can use your dice in these ways:

Precision Performer. Whenever you make a performance, deception, persuasion, intimidation, or acrobatics check, you can roll die and add it to the total. The die is only expended if you then succeed.

Performance of Battle. Once on your turn When you make an attack roll, you can roll a die and add to the total. The die is only expended if the attack hits.

Level 3: Battle Performance

As a bonus action, you can expend a performance die to begin a battle performance (unless you are wearing medium or heavy armor). The performance lasts until the end of your next turn, you're incapacitated, or you don medium or heavy armor. You can extend the performance by either using a bonus action to continue it, or moving at least 10 ft.

While the performance is active, you gain the following benefits.

Agility. Your movement speed increases by 10ft, and opportunity attack rolls have disadvantage against you. Additionally, you can make 1 unarmed strike as a bonus action.

Defense. You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your dexterity modifier.

Hops. You can use either strength or dexterity to calculate your jump height and distance (whichever is higher).

Level 9: Improved Performance

While your battle performance is active, you can use a bonus action to do one of the following actions.

Escape. You expend a performance die, roll it and add it to your AC until the start of your next turn, and either take the dash or disengage action.

Leap. You expend 5ft of your movement speed and jump adding a roll of your performance die to the height/distance. The dice are not expended.

Level 13: Performance of Attacks

While your battle performance is active, or otherwise expending a performance die, as a bonus action you can make either 2 unarmed strikes or 1 attack with a weapon.

Level 20: Master Performer

Once per turn when you roll a performance die choose one of the following options to do with it. You choose after you roll the die.

Luck. If it rolled a 1, you can reroll it, using the new roll.

Law. You take the average roll (rounded down) instead.

Preservation. If it rolled a 1 or 2, and the feature says you expend it, you don't expend it.

Expert. If the die rolled maximum, roll a d4 and add that to the total.

Variant Performer

All features are the same except Performance of Attacks; replace it with the following feature.

Level 13: Performance Maneuvers

Choose 5 maneuvers from the Battle Master Subclass; you know those maneuvers and can use them whenever. Use your performance dice when it mentions superiority dice.

The DC's equal 8 + your proficiency bonus + your strength or dexterity modifier (you choose which).

You can use one maneuver per turn, and the first one you use per long rest doesn't expend the die, provided your battle performance is active.

items.title: The Jack of All Jacks
items.html:
The Jack of All Jacks

Embrace being a jack of all trades to the nth degree.

Prerequisite: your 2 choices from dabbling in all classes being from different classes

Level 3: Dabbling in a Subclass

At 3rd level, you have even dabbled in different methods of executing the same abilities. Choose a 3rd level feature from any subclass, you gain that feature. You cannot choose one that mentions another class feature in which you do not have.

Other Jack of All Trades subclasses are recommended.

Level 3: Skill Specialist

You gain proficiency in heavy armor and 2 skills of your choice.

Level 9: Dabbled in a Few Subclasses

Choose a 9th or lower level feature from a subclass, you gain that feature. You cannot choose one that mentions another class feature in which you do not have, or is from the same subclass that you chose for Dabbling in a Subclass.

Other Jack of All Trades subclasses are recommended.

Level 13: Dabbled in Many Subclasses

Choose a 13th or lower level feature from a subclass, you gain that feature. You cannot choose one that mentions another class feature in which you do not have, or is from the same subclass that you chose for Dabbling in a Subclass or Dabbled in a Few Subclasses.

Other Jack of All Trades subclasses are recommended.

Level 20: Master of All Classes

Choose an additional feature from the Even More Dabbling in All Classes feature. You gain that feature; restrictions are as described in the Even More Dabbling in All Classes feature.
